b: Beta-globin genes are located on chromosome 11. A person normally has two beta-globin genes, one inherited from each parent.
Mutations may reduce beta-chain production (β⁺) or abolish it (β⁰). Clinical severity depends on the mutations inherited and other genetic modifiers.
The traditional clinical categories are beta thalassaemia minor, intermedia and major. These categories describe a clinical spectrum rather than three completely separate genetic conditions.

qs.q: A 10-year-old girl with beta-thalassaemia major receiving chronic transfusions develops cardiac failure and endocrine abnormalities. Which chelating agent strategy prevents ongoing tissue damage most effectively?
o: Using oral deferasirox to continuously bind excess iron deposits
Combining deferoxamine and deferiprone for rapid myocardial iron clearance
Applying subcutaneous deferoxamine infusions to clear liver stores
Administering oral deferiprone to target labile plasma iron fractions
Using high-dose ascorbic acid supplementation to mobilize iron pools
qs.e: Combination therapy with deferoxamine and deferiprone provides superior chelation for clearing high-risk cardiac iron overload.
